svg.text: A day in the life of a DPDK packet: RX and TX with the mlx5 PMD on a ConnectX NIC
RX (blue) climbs from the cable to the app. TX (orange) goes down from the app to the cable. No kernel, no interrupts, no copies on the packet path. Step numbers match the text.
your code reads each mbuf: parse, match rules, decide
runs forever at 100% CPU; no sleep, no syscalls
hands a batch of mbufs to the driver
reads new CQEs, fills mbuf fields, returns the batch
the CQs are never armed: the core polls instead
first frees old mbufs, then writes one WQE per packet
create queues and flow rules; the only
part that goes through the kernel
traffic not steered to DPDK still
ioctl, then mlx5_ib sends the firmware command
takes the next RQ WQE, writes the packet into that mbuf, then a CQE
reads the WQE, then the mbuf data, later writes a CQE
rte_flow rules steer packets to DPDK; RSS picks the RQ; checksums
checksums, TSO, VLAN, as the WQE asks
holds packets for the pipeline; if full: pause / PFC, or drop
picks which SQ sends next: QoS, rate limits, pause
runs the setup commands that came
RX: find the frame, check the FCS (CRC),
TX: add the preamble and the
RX: recover the clock, turn the signal into bits,
TX: encode, add FEC, turn bits
into an electrical or optical signal
Port: RJ45 (copper BASE-T) or SFP / QSFP / OSFP cage (DAC / optical)
dashed = read (DMA read or CPU poll)
WQE = work queue entry (a descriptor). CQE = completion queue entry. mbuf = DPDK's packet buffer. PMD = poll mode driver: the mlx5 driver that runs inside the app.
